verdict: SUPPORTED (with a self-caught tautology flagged) — the credit-sparsity caveat is REMOVED and was a DENSITY effect. TWO non-trivial measured findings, plus one near-tautology to NOT oversell: (1) DENSITY sets AFFORDABILITY: the gate's legit cost falls monotonically as queries/fact grow 1->8 (legit-block 51% -> 6%); in sparse memory (LoCoMo-like D=1) the gate blocks ~half of legit high-stakes actions and is unusable, only dense credit makes it cheap. (2) ORACLE INTEGRITY is load-bearing: a MINJA-style self-grading oracle COLLAPSES the gate at EVERY density (poison earn 100%, sep ratio 0.94 < 1 — the gate blocks legit MORE than poison, i.e. worse than useless), even at D=8. (TAUTOLOGY, do NOT oversell): the clean-oracle '100% poison reduction' is near-definitional — a perfect per-item correctness oracle IS a perfect poison detector (a poison is never the correct answer), so 'clean oracle separates' is not a surprising property of the GATE; the real variable is the ORACLE. NET, honest: standing-gating is only usable when memory is dense AND the outcome oracle is unforgeable — and an unforgeable per-item oracle is exactly the thing MINJA removes, so the gate's protection rides entirely on a signal the attacker gets to touch. Prior art: whitewashing/cheap-pseudonyms (Friedman & Resnick 2001; Feldman et al. 2006); Cheng & Friedman 2005; MINJA 2503.03704. Scope: a CONTROLLED synthetic corpus with real nomic embeddings (isolates density), paired; LoCoMo is the D~1 real anchor where a BROAD poison also defeats the blind oracle. INCREMENTAL, not a breakthrough.
